content.value:
Pedro Pathing gives you three ways to control heading along a path:

Constant — heading stays fixed. setConstantHeadingInterpolation(heading). Best for strafing sideways or keeping an intake aimed at the field.

Linear — heading changes smoothly from start to end. setLinearHeadingInterpolation(start, end). Good for predictable turns.

Tangent — heading follows the curve's slope. setTangentHeadingInterpolation(). The robot faces the direction it's moving. Best for high-speed curves.

content.question: Which interpolation makes the robot face the direction it's traveling at every point?

content.value:
Open HeadingInterpolationOpMode.java.

The skeleton has a private Follower field.

Create the Follower with Constants.createFollower(hardwareMap). Set its pose with follower.setPose(new Pose(70.75, 70.75, 0)).

Position the robot: left-click drag near center, right-click to face 0° (right).

steps.title: Build a path with all three modes

content.value:
Starting from (70.75, 70.75, 0):

Segment 1: BezierLine to (142.75, 70.75, 0) with setConstantHeadingInterpolation(0) — drive right while facing right.

Segment 2: BezierLine to (142.75, 142.75, Math.toRadians(90)) with setLinearHeadingInterpolation(0, Math.toRadians(90)) — drive up while turning.

Segment 3: BezierCurve from there to (70.75, 70.75, 0) with control at (106.75, 106.75, 0) and setTangentHeadingInterpolation().

Add .setGlobalDeceleration() before .build().

Schedule: new FollowPathCommand(follower, chain).

Start the OpMode.

Segment 1: robot drives right while facing right — constant heading.

Segment 2: robot smoothly turns while driving diagonally — linear interpolation.

Segment 3: robot follows the curved path, facing its direction of travel — tangent.
